statement: The ko-KR language pack's terminology table holds 11 entries, all finance or AI. Generating the unseen-topic holdout on Seoul housing supply required 착공, 준공 and 인허가 — the three terms the whole piece turns on — and none of them is in the pack. The child variant therefore carries glosses the Writer coined ('공사를 시작하는 날', '공사가 다 끝나서 집이 완성되는 날', '정부가 땅에 집을 지어도 좋다고 허락하는 것') with no terminology authority behind them. The glosses read correctly, which is precisely the risk: an unbacked coinage that happens to be right is indistinguishable in the output from one that is wrong. This is a coverage gap that only became visible because the holdout topic was chosen from outside the corpus's domain — on the two pilot topics the terminology table looked complete. Recorded at task_local scope: this is an agent observation, and basis "model_inference" may not carry scope "calibration_candidate" on its own — agent consensus never silently becomes durable preference. Promoting this finding into the pack requires the owner.

routing.rationale: editorial/feedback-routing.json's domain_terminology layer owns 'which term names the concept ... whether an audience-facing alias still maps to the same concept', and its repair says an agent may not invent a canonical rendering. That is exactly what happened here. It is not an audience-layer finding: the reading level was fine and the simplification was appropriate — what is missing is the authority backing the mapping. Not routed to verification either, since no claim changed meaning.
